bull.b: Autoship represented 84.4% of Q1 net sales and grew more than 10% year over year, giving Chewy a large recurring purchasing base. Because pet food and other consumables require replenishment, this mix can support repeat order frequency, demand visibility, and customer retention over coming quarters.

Consistently positive operating and free cash flow, with free cash flow sizeable relative to reported earnings, supports earnings quality and gives Chewy internally generated funds for technology, fulfillment, customer acquisition, and strategic expansion. This improves resilience as the business scales.

SmartPak and Modern Animal broaden Chewy beyond its core online assortment into specialized nutrition and veterinary care. The planned roughly 60 clinics and approximately $290 million of steady-state clinic revenue contribution could deepen customer engagement, expand the addressable market, and diversify future growth.

bear.b: Management's more conservative FY2026 sales outlook, at 6.3%–7.5% growth, indicates that near-term demand assumptions have weakened. Slower growth can reduce operating leverage and make the company more dependent on execution, acquisitions, and margin initiatives to sustain its longer-term earnings trajectory.

Lower expected customer additions and softer premiumization and attach rates could limit the expansion of Chewy's customer base and spend per customer. These trends may constrain revenue acceleration and reduce the operating leverage available from the platform, even if existing recurring purchases remain resilient.

Although recent leverage is described as manageable, debt-to-equity is around 1.1 and equity has been volatile and relatively small versus assets. A historically stretched capital structure can amplify business swings, limit flexibility during weaker periods, and increase the importance of sustained cash generation.
